newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX soars to third closing high in a row.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX soars to third closing high in a row.

text.p: The Hungarian share market's BUX index coasted to a third successive closing high on Friday with no specific news to support the continuing rally, traders and analysts said.
"It was a really good day, the turnover was good again but there was no specific news," said Andrea Keresztesi, a trader for ABN Amro Hoare Govett in Budapest.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary third consecutive closing high of 7,605.60 points, up 54.76 or 0.73 percent.
Frances Cloud, an analyst for Nomura Equity Research in London, said the Hungarian and Russian bourses were benefitting from investors looking for places to put their money in the region.

"Currently Russia and Hungary are the top picks. Russia, I guess mainly because it's so liquid and everyone's so blindly optimistic about it, and Hungary because it's the one country in Central Europe which actually has an improving macreconomic situation," Cloud said.
"Everyone's just stuffing their money into the same old sort of blue chips...(but) I don't think the fundamentals are as good as the share prices by any means."

Keresztesi said some issues, notably Zalakeramia, rose because investors were looking for something new to buy after shunning them earlier in the week. The tilemaking company rose 345 forints to close at 8,240 on a relatively heavy volume of 37,492 shares traded.
Danubius, which rose sharply on Wednesday and Thursday, was off in early trade on profit-taking but partially recovered at the close on the basis of a block sale, traders said.
Twenty-one stocks plus the compensation coupon ended higher, nine were lower and six were unchanged. Volume of traded stocks and coupons amounted to a relatively light 990,982 units.
